title: Insight Apply Rewind: interactive diff preview, staged safe-apply, and reconciliation timeline for Optimize
creator: Ava Kim
description: Purpose: Provide a single, developer-friendly surface in Console Optimize that lets customers preview batching/caching recommendations, simulate and stage safe configuration applies, and inspect a time-ordered reconciliation ledger that fully explains what changed, who applied it, and how to rollback. This ticket covers the UX flows, acceptance criteria, and handoff artifacts for engineering and design. Goals: reduce manual config churn, lower per-token costs by surfacing safe batching/caching deltas, and make rollbacks trivial for operators. Scope: recommendation cards with inline modeled impact, an interactive diff preview modal with toggles for each change (batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile), staged apply workflow with canary/auto-rollback options, and an immutable apply history view with expanded entries for diagnostics and links to telemetry. Out of scope: backend orchestration engine changes to perform automatic quantization; those are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display predicted token savings and SLO risk score inline (values from Optimize engine), with CTA to preview
Diff preview modal shows field-level changes, estimated cost delta, sample response tokenization differences, and a toggleable safe-apply option (canary percent + duration)
Staged apply flow supports: preview -> schedule (immediate or delayed) -> canary rollout -> automatic rollback on defined SLI regressions; backend hooks exist (API contract) and UX surfaces job state

Apply history (ledger) is queryable by time range and user, shows before/after snapshots, linked telemetry (latency/cost dashboards) and provides single-click rollback that creates a reverse staged apply
All actions are auditable: every apply has an immutable entry with actor, timestamp, commit SHA (if from CI), and optional changelog message
Design reviewed and approved by Product + Security; engineering has acceptance tests and e2e playbook for rollback testing
Feature toggles allow gradual rollout to accounts (beta flag) and telemetry events fire for exposure/accept/rollback for product metrics
